# Template: molecule_3d
A ball-and-stick molecule drawn in 3D perspective (static viewpoint, flat sketchy rendering): preset geometries for methane (tetrahedral), water (bent), ammonia (pyramidal) and CO₂ (linear), with adjustable camera angles. Choose this scene for requests about molecular SHAPE — tetrahedral geometry, bond angles, VSEPR, "show methane in 3D", lone-pair geometry discussions. For flat structural formulas of arbitrary molecules use the chemistry pack's molecule template instead. Rotate the whole molecule smoothly with the animate command: {"animate": {"azimuth": 240}, "duration": 3} (write the starting azimuth in params).
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "molecule": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "methane",
    "water",
    "ammonia",
    "co2"
   ],
   "description": "Which preset geometry (default methane)."
  },
  "azimuth": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Camera orbit angle in degrees (default 28)."
  },
  "elevation": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Camera tilt in degrees (default 18)."
  },
  "show_labels": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Element symbols next to the atoms (default true)."
  },
  "name": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "Caption, e.g. \"Methane CH₄ — tetrahedral, 109.5°\". A sensible default is provided per molecule."
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- molecule: SET — the whole model in one id (spheres, sticks, symbols, shadow), e.g. draw [molecule]
- atom_0: the central atom's sphere
- atom_<i>: the outer atoms' spheres (i = 1…)
- bond_<i> / bond_<i>__f: the two depth-sorted halves of each stick
- label_<i>: the element symbol next to atom i (when show_labels)
- caption: the caption line under the figure
Examples:
Request: "Show methane in 3D so the tetrahedral shape is clear." → params: {"molecule":"methane","azimuth":32}
Request: "Show the bent shape of a water molecule." → params: {"molecule":"water","azimuth":40}

In YAML: `template: molecule_3d` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
